## Summary: cmux-companion

### 1. What It Does
**cmux-companion** is an iPhone companion app for [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux), a Mac terminal multiplexer. It bridges your iPhone to cmux running on your Mac via a local network connection, enabling remote control and real-time notifications of terminal activity from your phone.

**Architecture**: Mac app → Unix socket → Go bridge (cmux-bridge) → WebSocket/LAN → iOS app

### 2. Target Audience
- **cmux users** who want to control their terminal multiplexer from their iPhone while on the same local network
- **Terminal power users and developers** who need quick access to workspace/surface controls without physically being at their Mac
- Primarily iOS 17+ users on macOS 13+

### 3. Key Features / Unique Selling Points
- **Voice commands**: Send text input via speech recognition to any surface
- **Volume button shortcuts**: Landscape-optimized controls (single/double-press) for cycling surfaces, workspaces, opening quick actions
- **Real-time notifications**: Mirror cmux notifications to iPhone with local push alerts
- **Workspace/surface management**: Select workspaces, focus surfaces, create/split/close terminals remotely
- **Quick actions menu**: Access common terminal operations (Enter, Ctrl+C, Tab, Arrow keys, Split Right/Down, New Terminal, Workspace creation)
- **Bonjour discovery**: Auto-discover bridge on LAN; secure QR-code pairing
- **Pane visualization**: Display actual pane layouts on iPhone reflecting Mac terminal state
- **Landscape-first design** with minimal on-screen controls

### 4. Tech Stack
- **iOS App**: SwiftUI (iOS 17+), Combine framework, UserNotifications API
- **Bridge**: Go 1.21+ (WebSocket server, Unix socket client, mDNS/Bonjour, QR generation)
- **Protocol**: JSON-RPC over WebSocket with Bearer token auth
- **Deployment**: LaunchAgent for macOS auto-start

**Key components**:
- `/ios/cmux/` - SwiftUI views (Layout, Control, Input, Connection, Pairing, Notifications, Settings)
- `/bridge/` - Go binary with internal packages (socket, WebSocket, poller, mDNS, pairing)
- `/shared/` - WebSocket protocol specification

message.content: should I use the same video from instagram/tiktok for twitter or should I just post a picture? or maybe abreviated video

content.text:
For Twitter/X, I'd go with an **abbreviated video (15-30 seconds)** — here's why:

- **Video outperforms images** on X for engagement and algorithmic reach, especially for tech demos
- But X users scroll faster than TikTok/IG — you need to hook in the **first 3 seconds**
- The full TikTok/IG video is likely too long for X attention spans

**My recommendation:**

Cut the TikTok/IG video down to the **single best "wow" moment** — probably the voice command sending text to the terminal, or the volume button workspace switching. No intro, no setup, just the payoff.

**Format:**
- 15-30 seconds max
- Start mid-action (no "hey guys" opener)
- Silent-friendly — X autoplays muted, so the visual should make sense without audio
- Let the tweet text do the explaining, let the video do the showing

**What NOT to do:**
- Don't post just a screenshot — it undersells the interactivity which is the whole point
- Don't repost the full TikTok with the watermark — X deprioritizes that in the algorithm

message.content: when replying to andrew chens tweet, should I link my tweet or the github repo or both?

content.text:
Link **your tweet** — not the repo directly.

**Why:**
- Your tweet has the video + context + narrative. The repo alone is cold and technical.
- If Andrew or his audience engages with your reply, the algorithm boosts **your tweet** — which already links to the repo. Double exposure.
- A GitHub link in a reply looks spammy. A quote or "I just posted about this" with a link to your own tweet feels like a natural conversation.

**Something like:**
> Built an open source iPhone companion for a terminal multiplexer — voice commands, volume button shortcuts, the works. Just shared it here: [link to your tweet]

Keep it short and relevant to whatever Andrew's tweet was about. Don't oversell — let curiosity do the work.
